subject: Atlas Labs renewal — dedicated capacity augmentation & credit request
messages:
From: Vikram Shah <vikram@atlaslabs.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlaslabs.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal & pool expansion — proposed numbers + credit ask

Hi Evelyn,

Quick note following our renewal planning call: Atlas is prepared to renew our Dedicated pool, but usage has grown faster than we forecasted. We want to move from a 4-GPU reserved pool to an initial 10-GPU pool (NVIDIA A100 class equivalence) with a planned scale to 14 GPUs post-q1.

Primary asks:
- A short-term credit to offset migration/onboarding costs and delta vs. spot during the ramp (we were hoping for a one-time credit applied to the first invoice).
- A firm throughput guarantee for sustained production traffic (we need >120 tokens/sec aggregate, 99th pctl latency target).

I'm attaching our Q2 usage export and a PO draft. Can your team put a proposal on the table this week? We are targeting signatures before Aug 20 to align budget cycles.

Thanks,
Vikram
Vikram Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, Atlas Labs
(Attachment: Atlas_usage_Q2_2027.csv)
(Attachment: Atlas_PO_draft_2027.pdf)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Vikram Shah <vikram@atlaslabs.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & pool expansion — proposed numbers + credit ask

Vikram — thanks for the details and the attachments. Appreciate the target timeline.

We can support the 10 -> 14 GPU runway; a couple of quick clarifications before I take this to pricing/finance:
- Is the 14-GPU target a hard requirement by Q1 or a stretch target you want optional capacity for?
- Are you open to a longer-term commit (24 months) in exchange for a bigger onboarding/term credit?

Prelim thinking from our side: 1) 12-month renewal with a one-time onboarding credit (single invoice credit) or 2) larger credit if Atlas signs a 24-month commitment and agrees to the throughput SLA (we'd bake an SLO into the renewal). I'll assemble two proposal lanes and loop in Markus for exec sign-off if we need an exception beyond standard discounts.

I should have the draft quote and an internal approval ask today.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: —)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Atlas Labs renewal — credit ask (exec approval needed)

Markus / team — forwarding Atlas' ask. Key points: 4 -> 10 GPUs now, plan to 14; requests a one-time credit against onboarding/delta costs; needs throughput SLO (>=120 tokens/sec aggregate, 99th pctl latency target). They want to sign by Aug 20.

Proposal (two lanes):
A) 12-month term: 10 GPU reserved pool, option to top up. One-time onboarding credit: 10% off first-month invoice. Standard SLO language.
B) 24-month term: commit to 12 GPUs initial reserved, planned increase to 14 at month 6. One-time onboarding + term credit: 18% applied as a combination of first invoice credit + annual rebate. Include explicit throughput SLO and automatic fallback routing to a compatible model family during partial outages.

Asking for exec approval to offer lane B up to 18% OR a middle ground concession if needed. Note: Atlas is price-sensitive but strategic (pilot already powers two flagship features). If we can get 24 months and a higher commit, it materially improves capacity planning.

Attachments: Atlas_usage_Q2_2027.csv (for context)

--Evelyn
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Atlas Labs renewal — credit ask (exec approval needed)

Evelyn — appreciate the clear lanes. Quick take: we can approve a one-time credit up to 15% total value contingent on the following being contractually committed: 1) 24-month term, 2) minimum initial reserved capacity of 12 GPUs, 3) defined throughput SLO (>=120 tokens/sec aggregate with 99p latency target) and 4) explicit escalation & remediation steps in the SLA (fallback models, regional burst policy).

If Atlas will not do 24 months, approve up to 8% as a one-time onboarding credit for a 12-month term. Keep the offer granular so finance can model the ARR hit.

Markus
Markus Klein
SVP, Commercial — Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Vikram Shah <vikram@atlaslabs.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@atlaslabs.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & pool expansion — proposed numbers + credit ask

Vikram — thanks for the patience. We reviewed internally and can make the following commercial offer:

Offer (conditional):
- 24-month committed term
- Initial reserved capacity: 12 GPUs, planned rollover to 14 GPUs at month 6
- One-time credit equal to 15% of the first year committed value, applied as a credit on invoice #1
- Throughput SLO: sustained aggregate >=120 tokens/sec; 99th pctl latency target included in SLA language
- SLA includes automated fallback to compatible model variants and a regional burst policy for short windows (details in quote)

To proceed: sign the attached updated quote and return the PO by Aug 20. DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/XYZ-Atlas-2027. I'll attach the quote (Atlas_renewal_quote_v2.pdf).

If Atlas prefers a 12-month term instead, the maximum one-time credit we can apply is 8% — let me know and I can update the quote accordingly.

Thanks — hope this lands close to what you need.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Atlas_renewal_quote_v2.pdf)
From: Vikram Shah <vikram@atlaslabs.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlaslabs.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & pool expansion — proposed numbers + credit ask

Evelyn — that looks workable. Atlas will commit to 24 months with the 12 -> 14 GPU plan. We accept the 15% one-time credit and the SLO conditions, subject to two small clarifications:
1) Can the regional burst policy include a 48-hour buffer window for unplanned traffic spikes during the transition?
2) Please confirm the credit will be applied as a line-item credit on invoice #1 (we need this for internal accounting).

We'll sign the DocuSign once those two bullet points are confirmed. Please include the PO instructions in your email to procurement.

Thanks — Vikram
